newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd Q3 expected to gain from shipping.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd Q3 expected to gain from shipping.

text.p: Shipping, which hit rock bottom for Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV in 1995, should be the key to slightly improved profits in the third quarter this year, analysts said.
Forecasts of Nedlloyd's net profit in the three months to September range from 20 million to 34 million guilders, against 23 million last year. Nedlloyd issues its figures on November 27.
Analysts say Nedlloyd's improved and restructured shipping division will explain the profit growth.
"Our estimates are based on the recovery of the operating result of shipping," said Thibaud de Guerre, ING Barings' head of equity research.
Shipping growth will be due to the company's Global Alliance, healthier volumes and cost reductions.
However, as some analysts point out, the figures will only indicate a gain relative to the trough of 1995. In absolute terms, Nedlloyd still faced a tough battle.
The company will have suffered from increasing competition and tariff erosion on many of its routes.
"P&O said there was considerable pressure on Europe/Far East routes which should have some impact....this represents 40 percent (of Nedlloyd's shipping business)," said Andre Mulder, analyst at BZW.
One bit of fortune for Nedlloyd was the guilder's depreciation against the dollar in the quarter.
"The dollar has been sliding for years, but for once, Nedlloyd will have benefitted," said Gert Jochems of NIB Strating.
In Nedlloyd's land activities, European Transport and Distribution, analysts predict stablity or slight improvement, partly as cost cutting takes effect.
"There's also been growth of about seven percent in road transport (in northwest Europe)," said Bert van Hoogenhuyze of Amstgeld.

Nedlloyd, however, will be unable to rely on the profitable Neddrill. The unit's sale to Noble Drilling Corp was completed in the second quarter. Last year the division contributed 8 million guilders in the third quarter.
The merger of its container business with Peninsular and Orient, formalised this week, is also yet to take effect.
